marks.gloss_en: נאמר מועדו בפסח ונאמר מועדו בתמיד: מה מועדו האמור בתמיד דוחה את השבת, אף מועדו האמור בפסח דוחה את השבת. Narrated first (66a.4) but argued SECOND per the stam's 66a.11 reconstruction (והדר אמר להו גזירה שוה); it is the derivation that stands
the daily tamid offering overrides Shabbat -- the source-side premise both derivations lean on (the two-hundred pesachim of 66a.3 are the year's tamid and musaf offerings)

ועוד, קל וחומר הוא: ומה תמיד שאין ענוש כרת דוחה את השבת, פסח שענוש כרת אינו דין שדוחה את השבת. ONE middah, TWO loci: uttered at 66a.5, re-quoted by the stam at 66a.11 (אמר מר: ועוד קל וחומר) -- not double-minted (predeclared). Per the stam's reconstruction it was argued FIRST: קל וחומר אמר להו ברישא ופרכוה

איכא למיפרך: מה לתמיד שכן תדיר וכליל — the tamid is both constant and wholly burnt, stringencies the pesach lacks, so its Shabbat-override cannot be exported a fortiori. Voiced by the stam at 66a.11 and, in the narrative, by the Bnei Beteira themselves at 66a.12: אמרו ליה קל וחומר פריכא הוא (ופרכוה, 66a.11). UNANSWERED -- the KV dies; the GS block carries no trace of this ground. tadir/kalil are declared gloss-only debt (trigger: a Zevachim תדיר וקודם sugya; and `kalil` already names a different, Chullin-24a sense)
ותמיד גופיה מנלן דדחי שבת? אילימא משום דכתיב ביה במועדו — פסח נמי הא כתיב ביה מועדו! if מועדו itself carried the override, the Bnei Beteira would have needed no Hillel for the pesach either

אלא מועדו לא משמע ליה, הכא נמי מועדו לא משמע להו: אלא אמר קרא עולת שבת בשבתו על עולת התמיד — מכלל דתמיד קרבה בשבת (= p_olat_shabbat): the word did not signify to them; the premise rests on the explicit verse
'the Shabbat olah on its Shabbat, beside the olah of the tamid' -- by implication, the tamid is offered on Shabbat: the verse that actually grounds the premise
the paschal offering overrides Shabbat -- Hillel's conclusion, held by both derivations and finally by the Bnei Beteira

one may not derive a gezera shava on his own authority -- the principle that explains why the Bnei Beteira could not have reached the GS unaided, and why Hillel offered them the KV they COULD have derived. A principle prop plus glosses, not a restrictions: block (predeclared): it does not bar this GS, which Hillel held by reception from Shemaya and Avtalyon
leave Israel be: if they are not prophets, they are sons of prophets -- Hillel's warrant for letting the forgotten halakha surface from practice

one who forgot to bring a knife before Shabbat: if his pesach is a lamb he sticks it in its wool, if a kid, between its horns -- the halakha Hillel had heard and forgotten (הלכה זו שמעתי ושכחתי, 66a.7)
